mainTopic: What ruins the קומץ, how the קמיצה is done, and how changes to a מנחה's oil or לבונה disqualify it
overview: The amud opens at the end of a משנה: a pebble, salt, or לבונה that comes up with the קומץ makes the מנחה פסול. The גמרא explains why all three examples are needed. It then explains why the משנה blames a קומץ that is חסר or יתר rather than חציצה: the item may be off to the side. אביי and רבא discuss how the קומץ is taken, and a ברייתא confirms that the כהן bends three fingers over his palm and levels the handful with his thumb and little finger. The גמרא calls this one of the hardest עבודות in the מקדש. רב פפא and מר בר רב אשי then ask about unusual ways of doing קמיצה, חפינה, and putting the קומץ into a כלי, and every question ends in תיקו. A new משנה rules that too much oil, too little oil, or too little לבונה makes a מנחה פסולה. רבי אליעזר explains 'too much oil' as two לוגין set aside for it, and the גמרא defends his reading from the word 'its oil.' Finally, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree about how little לבונה may remain.

steps.title: End of the משנה: a pinch of לבונה invalidates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the last item from the משנה's list: if a pinch of לבונה came up in the קומץ, the מנחה is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or a pinch of לבונה came up in his hand, the offering is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the משנה's list so it can ask about it. This line sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full list in the משנה is a pebble, a grain of salt, or a pinch of לבונה. If any of these came up with the קומץ, the handful does not have the right amount of flour, so the מנחה is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense, placed on top of the מנחה
The handful of flour the כהן takes from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח

phrases.english: Or a pinch of frankincense, it is invalid.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: An outside item (pebble, salt, or לבונה) in the קומץ makes the מנחה פסול.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need all three examples?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה lists three items when one example would teach the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need all of these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה bothered to list a pebble, salt, and לבונה, since any one of them shows that the קומץ must be a full measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes a משנה does not waste words. If all three items work the same way, listing each one seems extra. So it wants to know what each example adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need all these? The standard question when a list looks repetitive

phrases.english: Why do I need all these?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the length of the list just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of the three examples adds

steps.title: Salt is needed beyond the pebble
steps.stepSummary: צריכא: if the משנה had taught only a pebble, we would say salt does not ruin the measure, because salt itself is offered on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If it had taught only a pebble, I would say that is because a pebble is not something offered on the מזבח. But salt is offered, so I might say the קומץ stays valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by showing why salt has to be listed in addition to the pebble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pebble obviously does not belong in an offering, so of course it counts against the measure. Salt is put on the קומץ before it is burned, so we might have counted it as part of the offering. The משנה lists salt to teach that it still makes the קומץ פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary: each case teaches something the others cannot
Something that gets offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: It is necessary.
For if it had taught a pebble,
that is because it is not something offered,
phrases.notes: Meaning, that is the only reason a pebble ruins the קומץ.

phrases.english: but salt, which is something offered,
I would say it should be valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with the first half of a צריכא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Salt is listed because, unlike a pebble, it is offered, so we might have thought it does not reduce the measure.

steps.title: לבונה is needed beyond salt
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only salt, we would say לבונה does not ruin the measure, because לבונה is placed on the whole מנחה from the start. So the משנה teaches all three.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught only salt, I would say that is because salt is not set with the whole מנחה from the beginning, since only the קומץ is salted. But לבונה is set with the whole מנחה from the beginning, so I might say the קומץ stays valid. The משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא by showing why לבונה must be listed in addition to salt, then concludes that all three are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salt touches only the קומץ, so it is less tied to the מנחה. לבונה sits on the whole מנחה before the קמיצה, so we might have treated it as part of the מנחה and not counted it against the measure. The משנה teaches that even לבונה makes the קומץ פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Salt, put on the קומץ before it is burned
Was fixed or set together with
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: Each item has its own reason to seem harmless: salt is offered, and לבונה sits on the whole מנחה. Still, all of them make the קומץ פסול.

phrases.english: And if it had taught salt,
that is because it was not set with the meal offering from the beginning
(for he salts only the handful),
phrases.notes: Some versions have these words in round brackets and some don't. Either way, they explain that only the קומץ gets salted.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לְבוֹנָה דְּאִיקְּבַע בַּהֲדֵי מִנְחָה מֵעִיקָּרָא –
phrases.english: but frankincense, which was set with the meal offering from the beginning,
I would say it should be valid.
So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכא begun in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לבונה is listed because, unlike salt, it is set with the whole מנחה, so we might have thought it does not reduce the measure.

steps.title: The משנה's reason: a short or oversized handful is invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's reason: these items disqualify because a קומץ that is too small or too big is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they said: a handful that is lacking or extra is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the reason the משנה gives for its ruling. This line sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה explains the ruling through the measure. The outside item either takes up room, so there is less flour, or it adds to the handful, so the amount is wrong. Either way the קומץ is not exact.

keyTerms.meaning: Lacking, less than the required amount
Extra, more than the required amount

phrases.english: Because they said:
The handful that is lacking or extra is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ: הַקּוֹמֶץ הֶחָסֵר אוֹ הַיָּתֵר פָּסוּל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קומץ that is too small or too big is פסול.

steps.title: Why not say the problem is a barrier?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה blames a wrong measure, when the item could disqualify simply as חציצה between the כהן's hand and the flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically because of חסר or יתר? Let it get the ruling from חציצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason the משנה chose, suggesting a simpler one: the item blocks the hand from the flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a pebble or salt is in the כהן's hand, it seems to stand between his hand and the flour. That alone should make the קמיצה פסול. So why does the משנה need the measure argument?

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? Why pick this reason?
Let him get it from (another, simpler reason)
A barrier between the hand and what it holds

phrases.english: Why specifically because of lacking or extra?
Let it get the ruling from interposition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason quoted in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's explanation that the item disqualifies because of חסר or יתר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חציצה looks like a more obvious reason to disqualify, so the measure reason seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The item may be off to the side
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the case is where the item sits at the side of the קומץ, so it is not a barrier. Only the measure problem applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: from the side.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה explains why the משנה uses the measure reason: the item can be at the side of the handful, not between the hand and the flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חציצה only applies when something comes between the hand and the flour. If the pebble or salt is on the side, nothing is blocked, yet it still takes up space in the handful. So the only reason that covers every case is that the קומץ is חסר or יתר.

keyTerms.meaning: From the side, at the edge of the handful and not between hand and flour

steps.whatToRemember: An outside item in the קומץ disqualifies because it throws off the measure. That reason works even when the item is at the side and is not a barrier.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה is not saying חציצה does not disqualify. He is saying the משנה chose a reason that works in every case, including the side case where there is no barrier.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
From the side.
phrases.notes: He means the item sits at the edge of the handful, so it isn't blocking the hand from the flour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case narrowly (the item is at the side)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The item always stands between hand and flour, so חציצה would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The item can be at the side, where there is no חציצה, so the משנה relies on the measure reason, which covers every case.

steps.title: אביי asks how the handful is taken
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבא how a כהן is supposed to take the קומץ from a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: How does one take the handful?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. אביי asks רבא for the practical method of taking the קומץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא discussed what ruins the size of the קומץ. Now it asks a hands-on question: how exactly does the hand grab the flour? This question sets up רבא's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Take a קומץ, a handful of flour from the מנחה

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rava:
How does one take the handful?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרָבָא: כֵּיצַד קוֹמְצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what disqualifies the קומץ to how the קומץ is physically taken.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct hand position for taking the קומץ.

steps.title: רבא: the way people normally grab a handful
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the קומץ is taken the ordinary way people take a handful.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The way people take a handful.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי: there is no special technique. The כהן simply grabs a handful the way anyone would.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When people grab a handful, they close all their fingers over their palm. So רבא's answer means the whole hand, little finger included, closes on the flour. That detail is what אביי will attack next.

keyTerms.meaning: The way they take a handful

phrases.english: He said to him:
As people take a handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קומץ is taken in the normal way people grab a handful, with all the fingers closed.

steps.title: אביי objects: each finger has its own job
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects from a ברייתא that gives each finger a separate מצוה role, with the קמיצה linked to the fourth finger and not the little finger.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection to him: This one is for the span, this one is for the handful. This one is for the cubit, this one is the finger, this one is the thumb.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא from a ברייתא that points to each finger and names its מצוה job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the little finger to measuring a זרת and gives the next finger to the קמיצה. That suggests the קמיצה starts from the fourth finger and leaves the little finger out. But רבא said to grab with the whole hand, the way people normally do.

keyTerms.meaning: A span, measured from the thumb to the little finger
The act of taking the handful; here, the finger it starts from
A cubit, measured to the tip of the middle finger
The pointer finger, used to sprinkle blood

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
This one is for the span, this one is for the handful.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is pointing at the fingers one by one, starting from the little finger.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ אַמָּה, זוֹ אֶצְבַּע, זוֹ גּוּדָל.
phrases.english: This one is for the cubit, this one is the finger, this one is the thumb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that the קומץ is taken with the whole hand, as people normally grab.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives the little finger a different job (the זרת), so it seems the little finger is not part of the קמיצה.

steps.title: The little finger is used for leveling
steps.stepSummary: The little finger is part of the קמיצה only to level it: the כהן takes a full handful and then wipes off the extra with his little finger from below.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is for leveling (that is, he takes a full handful so that it will not be lacking, and afterward he wipes off the extra with the little finger from below).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's objection. The little finger does play a role, but only to level off the handful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן first grabs with his whole hand so the קומץ will not be too small. Then he uses the little finger to wipe away what sticks out at the bottom, so it will not be too big. So רבא's 'normal grab' still stands, and the ברייתא simply did not list leveling as a separate job.

keyTerms.meaning: Wipes off the excess, scrapes level

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן grabs a full handful so it is not too small, then levels it with the little finger so it is not too big.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mean the little finger is uninvolved. It is involved, but only for leveling, not for the main grab.

phrases.english: Rather, it is for leveling,
phrases.notes: He means the little finger: its part in the קמיצה is only to even out the handful.

phrases.english: (that is, he takes a handful with a full hand
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: so that it will not be lacking,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מוֹחֵק בְּאֶצְבַּע קְטַנָּה מִלְּמַטָּה).
phrases.english: and afterward he wipes off the extra with the little finger from below).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection and keeps רבא's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the little finger's role so that the ברייתא and רבא do not conflict.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that the little finger plays no part in the קמיצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The little finger does play a part, but only to level off the handful.

steps.title: How exactly is the handful taken?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact way the קמיצה is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact hand movement of the קמיצה. This question sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we know only a general picture: a full grab, then leveling. Now the גמרא wants the precise position of the fingers.

phrases.english: How does he do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the precise method after the general picture was settled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact finger position for taking the קומץ.

steps.title: רב: bend three fingers onto the palm
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא בר טוביה quotes רב: the כהן bends his three fingers until they reach his palm, and that is how he takes the קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said that רב said: He bends his three fingers until they reach onto his palm, and takes the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the exact method: the כהן curls his three middle fingers down onto his palm and scoops up the flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The handful is the flour held between the three bent fingers and the palm. The thumb and little finger are not part of the main grab. This fits the earlier step, where the little finger is used only for leveling.
steps.whatToRemember: The קומץ is taken with the three middle fingers bent onto the palm. The little finger only helps level it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Toviyya said that Rav said:
He bends his three fingers,
phrases.notes: These are the three middle fingers, not the thumb or the little finger.

phrases.english: until they reach onto the palm of his hand,
and he takes the handful.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה, אָמַר רַב: חוֹפֶה שְׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how the קמיצה is done.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כהן bends his three middle fingers until they reach his palm, and so takes the קומץ.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב: three fingers bent over the palm
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'מלא קמצו' and 'בקמצו' together. The קומץ is neither overflowing nor a fingertip pinch. The כהן bends three fingers over his palm.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way: 'His full handful.' Could it be heaped and overflowing? The verse says 'in his handful.' If 'in his handful,' could it be with just his fingertips? The verse says 'his full handful.' So how is it done? He bends his three fingers over his palm and takes the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב said in step 13. This gives רב's description a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק stops a mistake the other could cause. 'מלא' alone might mean a heaped-up pile, so 'בקמצו' limits it to what is inside the closed hand. 'בקמצו' alone might mean a tiny fingertip pinch, so 'מלא' demands a full hand. The middle path is three fingers bent down onto the palm.

keyTerms.meaning: Heaped up, overflowing past the hand
Bends or covers (the fingers over the palm)

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns רב's practical description into a rule learned from the פסוקים themselves.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
phrases.notes: This backs up what רב said in step 13.

phrases.english: "His full handful"
Might it mean overflowing?
The verse says, "in his handful."
If it is "in his handful,"
might it be with his fingertips?
The verse says, "his full handful."
So how is it done?
He bends his three fingers
over the palm of his hand and takes the handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting רב's description in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רב's statement that the כהן bends three fingers to his palm
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'מלא קמצו' and 'בקמצו' together

steps.title: Wiping off the extra for pan offerings, the hard job
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. For a מחבת and מרחשת, the כהן wipes off extra flour with his thumb above and his little finger below. It calls this the hard עבודה in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a מחבת and a מרחשת, he wipes off the extra with his thumb from above and with his little finger from below. This is the hard עבודה in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going. It explains how the כהן levels the קומץ for two kinds of מנחה, then calls this the hardest job in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches step 11, where the little finger only levels the קומץ from below. Here the thumb also wipes from above. It is hard because he must remove just the extra and nothing from the קומץ itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A מנחה made in a flat pan
A מנחה made in a deep pan

phrases.english: With a pan offering and a deep-pan offering,
he wipes with his thumb from above
and with his little finger from below,
and this is the hard service in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and adds the wiping detail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For מחבת and מרחשת, the כהן levels the קומץ with his thumb above and little finger below. This is called the hard עבודה.

steps.title: Is this really the only hard job?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that מליקה and חפינה are also very hard Temple jobs.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one and no other? But there is pinching of a bird's neck, and there is scooping the incense!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's words 'the hard service.' Those words sound like nothing else is as hard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מליקה and חפינה are also known to be very hard. So calling קמיצה 'the' hard job seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Pinching the neck of a bird offering with the fingernail
The כהן גדול scooping incense with both hands on יום כיפור

phrases.english: This one, and no other?
But there is pinching!
And there is scooping!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's wording in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'וזו היא עבודה קשה שבמקדש'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other jobs (מליקה, חפינה) are also very hard. So קמיצה cannot be the one and only hard job.

steps.title: It is one of the hard jobs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: קמיצה is one of the hard jobs in the מקדש, not the only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is one of the hard עבודות in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection by adjusting the ברייתא's words to 'one of' the hard jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never meant that nothing else was hard. קמיצה joins מליקה and חפינה in a group of very hard jobs.
steps.whatToRemember: The קומץ is taken by bending three fingers over the palm. It must be full but not overflowing. For pan offerings, the extra is wiped off with the thumb above and little finger below. This is one of the hardest jobs in the מקדש, alongside מליקה and חפינה.

phrases.english: Rather, this is one
of the hard services in the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא זוֹ הִיא אַחַת מֵעֲבוֹדוֹת קָשׁוֹת שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls קמיצה the single hardest job.
steps.terutzMaskana: קמיצה is one of several hard jobs, along with מליקה and חפינה.

steps.title: The normal handful is the way people usually grab
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא states that it is obvious that 'מלא קמצו' means taking a handful the way people normally do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is obvious to me that 'his handful' means the way people normally take a handful.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא sets a simple starting point: the קומץ is taken the normal, everyday way people grab a handful. This prepares for his questions about unusual ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not spell out the exact hand motion, so רב פפא ties it to normal human behavior. That is the clear part. What happens when the כהן grabs in a strange way is what he asks next.

keyTerms.meaning: His full handful, the Torah's words for the קומץ of a מנחה
The way people normally take a handful

steps.confusionAlert: Saying the normal way is 'obvious' does not yet tell us that other ways are invalid. That is exactly what רב פפא asks next.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is obvious to me
that 'his handful' means the way people take a handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining how the כהן bends his fingers for the קומץ, רב פפא grounds the קומץ in normal human grabbing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'מלא קמצו' means a handful taken the way people normally take one.

steps.title: Unusual ways of taking the handful
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks about a קומץ taken with the fingertips, from the sides, or from below upward. The questions stay unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: If the כהן took the handful with his fingertips, what is the law? From the sides, what is the law? From below upward, what is the law? Let it stand unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks whether a קומץ taken in an odd way still counts. The גמרא cannot decide, so it says תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case still ends with flour in the כהן's hand, but not through the normal grabbing motion. The question is whether the Torah cares about the result (a handful) or the method (normal grabbing). No answer is found.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the קומץ is valid or invalid. It means the גמרא leaves the question open.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If he took the handful with his fingertips, what is the law?
From the sides, what is the law?
From below upward, what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: קָמַץ בְּרָאשֵׁי אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 'obvious' normal method by asking about methods that are not normal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a קומץ taken with the fingertips, from the sides, or from below upward valid?

steps.title: The normal scoop is the way people usually scoop
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא states that it is obvious that 'מלא חפניו' means scooping the way people normally scoop with both hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is obvious to me that 'his handfuls' means the way people normally scoop.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא now applies the same idea to חפינה, the two-handed scoop of קטורת. This sets up his next questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a parallel case. חפינה was mentioned in step 16 as another hard job in the מקדש. Just like קמיצה, its basic form is defined by how people normally scoop.

keyTerms.meaning: His full scooped handfuls (both hands together)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is obvious to me
that 'his handfuls' means the way people scoop.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:12, about the כהן גדול scooping קטורת on יום כיפור.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: פְּשִׁיטָא לִי, ״מְלֹא חׇפְנָיו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 18, moving from קמיצה to חפינה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'מלא חפניו' means scooping the way people normally scoop.

steps.title: Unusual ways of scooping the incense
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks about חפינה with fingertips, from the sides, or with each hand separately and then joined. The questions stay unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: If he scooped with his fingertips, what is the law? From the sides, what is the law? If he scooped with this hand and with that hand and then brought them together, what is the law? Let it stand unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks whether odd ways of scooping still count as חפינה. Again the גמרא says תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two cases match his קמיצה questions. The new case fits only חפינה, since it uses two hands. If each hand scoops alone and they are joined afterward, is that one real two-handed scoop or not? It stays unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: He scooped with each hand separately
He brought them close to each other

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If he scooped with his fingertips, what is the law?
From the sides, what is the law?
If he scooped with this hand and with that hand
and then brought them next to each other, what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: חָפַן בְּרָאשֵׁי אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 19, now for חפינה, adding a two-hand case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is חפינה valid if done with the fingertips, from the sides, or with separate hands joined afterward?

steps.title: A handful stuck to the wall of the vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether a קומץ stuck to the inner wall of the כלי counts as being in the כלי. The question stays unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: If he stuck the קומץ onto the wall of the vessel, what is the law? Do we need it to be inside the vessel, and here it is? Or perhaps we need it to be placed inside, and here it is not? Let it stand unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks about a קומץ put into the כלי that sticks to the side wall instead of resting inside. The גמרא lays out both sides and ends with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the קומץ is taken, it must be put into a כלי. The two sides: if the rule only needs the קומץ to be within the כלי, it is fine, since it is within the walls. If the rule needs the קומץ to be properly placed (resting) inside, then sticking to the wall is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The side wall of the vessel

steps.whatToRemember: All of רב פפא's questions here (odd ways of קמיצה, odd ways of חפינה, and a קומץ stuck to the כלי wall) end with תיקו. They are left open.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If he stuck the handful onto the side of the vessel, what is the law?
Do we need it inside the vessel, and here it is?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא הַנָּחָה בְּתוֹכוֹ בָּעֵינַן, וְלֵיכָּא?
phrases.english: Or perhaps we need it placed inside, and here it is not?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: דַּבְּקֵיהּ לְקוֹמֶץ בְּדַפְנֵיהּ דְּמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another question from רב פפא, now about the step after taking the קומץ: putting it into the כלי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a קומץ stuck to the wall of the כלי count as in the כלי? Is being inside enough, or must it be placed resting inside?

steps.title: A handful stuck to the bottom of an upside-down vessel
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי asks whether a קומץ stuck to the bottom of an overturned כלי counts as placed in the כלי. The question is left as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי asked: If the כהן turned the כלי upside down and stuck the קומץ to the bottom of the כלי, what is the law? Do we only need the קומץ to be placed in it, and that is true here? Or do we need it placed in it the normal way, and that is not true here? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: Following רב פפא's question about a קומץ stuck to the inside wall, מר בר רב אשי asks about a קומץ stuck to the bottom of a כלי that has been flipped over. Nobody answers, so the גמרא says תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question turns on what the rule of putting the קומץ into a כלי really demands. If any contact that counts as 'in the כלי' is enough, this works. If the כלי must be used the normal way, upright, then a flipped כלי does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: He turned the vessel upside down
Let it stand. The question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Steps 19 through 23 are a run of questions about unusual ways of doing קמיצה and putting it in a כלי. All of them stay unresolved.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi asked:
If he turned the vessel over,
and stuck the handful to the bottom of the vessel, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The קומץ is stuck to the floor of the כלי, but with the כלי upside down it hangs there instead of resting the normal way.

phrases.english: Do we require placing it inside, and that is present here,
or perhaps we require it the proper way, and that is not present?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב פפא's question about a קומץ stuck to the vessel's wall to a קומץ stuck to the bottom of a flipped vessel.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does placement in the כלי require only contact that counts as 'inside', or normal, upright use of the כלי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer is given. The question ends as תיקו.

steps.title: The משנה: how the handful is taken, and three disqualifications
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes how the כהן takes the קומץ. It then rules that a מנחה with extra oil, missing oil, or missing לבונה is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it? He stretches his fingers over the palm of his hand. If he added to its oil, took away from its oil, or took away from its לבונה, it is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains the physical method of קמיצה, and then lists three mistakes in the oil or לבונה that make the מנחה פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part answers 'how' with a hand position: the fingers are folded over the palm to scoop the flour. The second part says the amounts of oil and לבונה are fixed. Too much oil, too little oil, or too little לבונה ruins the offering.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the משנה lists 'too little לבונה' but not 'too much לבונה.' Only the oil is disqualified in both directions here.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
How does he do it?

phrases.aramaic: פּוֹשֵׁט אֶת אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו עַל פַּס יָדוֹ.
phrases.english: He extends his fingers onto the palm of his hand.
If he increased its oil, decreased its oil,
or decreased its frankincense, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the series of unresolved questions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קמיצה is done with the fingers folded over the palm. Extra oil, missing oil, or missing לבונה makes the מנחה פסולה.

steps.title: What counts as 'too much oil'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the משנה means when it says 'he increased its oil'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'he increased its oil'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking for the exact case of 'too much oil.' This sets up רבי אליעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding oil could happen in several ways, so the גמרא wants to pin down which situation the משנה is ruling on.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What are the circumstances of 'he increased its oil'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact meaning of the משנה's first disqualification.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific situation is meant by 'too much oil'?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: he set aside two לוגין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר explains that 'too much oil' means the כהן set aside two לוגין of oil for the מנחה instead of one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: For example, where he set aside two לוגין for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the question. The extra oil is a second לוג that was set aside for this מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחה normally gets one לוג of oil. In רבי אליעזר's case, all of the oil is sacred oil designated for this מנחה, but there is double the right amount.

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid measure. A מנחה gets one לוג of oil

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
For example, where he set aside two log for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כְּגוֹן שֶׁהִפְרִישׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי לוּגִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is one where two לוגין of oil were set aside for the מנחה instead of one.

steps.title: Why not a simpler case of outside oil?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר did not explain the משנה as a case where חולין oil, or oil from another מנחה, was mixed in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him explain it as a case where he mixed into it non-sacred oil, or the oil of another מנחה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's choice of case. It suggests a more obvious example of extra oil: oil that does not belong to this מנחה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two לוגין that were both set aside for this מנחה is an unusual case. The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר chose it over a plainer one, where foreign oil got mixed in.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him explain it as (a different case)

phrases.english: And let him explain it as where he mixed into it
non-sacred oil or the oil of another meal offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹקְמַהּ כְּגוֹן דְּעָרֵיב בָּהּ שֶׁמֶן דְּחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's choice of case in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's explanation that 'too much oil' means two לוגין set aside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler case is available, where outside oil is mixed in, so why choose the unusual two-לוגין case?

steps.title: Suggested defense: outside oil does not disqualify
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a possible answer: maybe חולין oil and another מנחה's oil do not disqualify, so רבי אליעזר could not use that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that non-sacred oil and the oil of another מנחה do not disqualify it,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible defense of רבי אליעזר. This line only proposes the idea, and it sets up the attack that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If oil that does not belong to the מנחה does not count as 'its oil,' then mixing it in would not make the מנחה פסולה. That would explain why רבי אליעזר needed a case where both לוגין were designated for this מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (a suggested answer)

phrases.english: And if you would say

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמֶן דְּחוּלִּין וָשֶׁמֶן דַּחֲבֶירְתַּהּ לָא פָּסֵל,
phrases.english: that non-sacred oil and the oil of another meal offering do not disqualify,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא שֶׁמֶן דְּחוּלִּין וָשֶׁמֶן דַּחֲבֶירְתַּהּ לָא פָּסֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggested legal distinction: only the מנחה's own oil disqualifies.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The outside-oil case seemed like a simpler example of 'too much oil.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Outside oil might not disqualify at all, so רבי אליעזר needed the two-לוגין case. This is only a suggestion and is attacked next.

steps.title: רב זוטרא בר טוביה: then how is מנחת חוטא disqualified by oil?
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא בר טוביה attacks the suggestion. If foreign oil does not disqualify, there would be no way to find the known case where oil disqualifies a מנחת חוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה objected: If so, regarding a מנחת חוטא, which oil disqualifies, how can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: רב זוטרא בר טוביה pushes back against the suggested defense from step 28. He points to מנחת חוטא, where we know oil makes the offering פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחת חוטא has no oil of its own, so any oil that disqualifies it must come from outside, such as חולין oil or another מנחה's oil. Since oil does disqualify it, outside oil must be able to disqualify. That knocks down the suggestion that it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it, attacked it
If so, then (introducing a problem that follows)
The meal offering brought by a poor sinner, which is brought without oil
How can you find such a case?

steps.whyThisMatters: The proof from מנחת חוטא shows that outside oil can disqualify a מנחה. So the original challenge from step 27 against רבי אליעזר comes back.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה:
phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Toviyya objected to this:
If that is so, the meal offering of a sinner,
in which oil disqualifies,
how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested defense of step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חולין oil and another מנחה's oil do not disqualify.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מנחת חוטא has no oil of its own, so the known rule that oil disqualifies it only works if outside oil can disqualify.

steps.title: Every possible source of oil in a מנחת חוטא is ruled out
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא בר טוביה spells out his attack. A מנחת חוטא has no oil of its own. If outside oil does not disqualify, then nothing could ever disqualify it through oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was the מנחה's own oil, a מנחת חוטא has no oil. If it was חולין oil or oil from another מנחה, you just said that kind of oil does not disqualify. And if you say he set aside oil especially for it, then since this מנחה has no oil at all, that oil is just חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זוטרא בר טוביה finishes his attack. He goes through every kind of oil that could get into a מנחת חוטא and shows that, under the suggestion, none of them could disqualify it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know oil does disqualify a מנחת חוטא, so some kind of oil must be able to do it. Its 'own' oil does not exist. Outside oil, under the suggestion of step 28, does not disqualify. Even oil set aside for it counts as ordinary חולין, because this מנחה is not supposed to have oil at all. So the suggestion leaves no case at all, and it must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: That of its fellow (oil belonging to another מנחה)

phrases.english: If its own oil – it does not have any,
if non-holy oil or the oil of another מנחה –
you just said it does not disqualify,
(and if you say that he set aside oil for it –
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in these round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: since it has no oil at all,
that oil is just non-holy).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the full reasoning of רב זוטרא בר טוביה's attack from step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion in step 28 that חולין oil or another מנחה's oil does not disqualify.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Process of elimination: own oil does not exist, outside oil would not disqualify, and designated oil counts as חולין. That leaves no way for the known rule (oil disqualifies a מנחת חוטא) to ever apply.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר chose the bigger surprise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that outside oil really does disqualify. רבי אליעזר picked the two-לוגין case because it is the case you would least expect to be disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר is speaking in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say that חולין oil or another מנחה's oil disqualifies. But if he set aside two לוגין for it, since this לוג is fit for it and that לוג is fit for it, you might say it should not be disqualified. So he teaches us that it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the suggestion from step 28 and gives a new answer to the question of step 27. Outside oil does disqualify. רבי אליעזר simply chose to teach the case that is harder to see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside oil obviously disqualifies, so teaching it adds little. In the two-לוגין case, each לוג on its own could have been the right oil for this מנחה, so you might think adding both is harmless. רבי אליעזר teaches that even this disqualifies, and the easier case of outside oil is understood automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No need to say': a style of teaching where the bigger case is said, and the easier case is understood from it
A measure of liquid (plural: לוגין); a regular מנחה gets one לוג of oil

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אליעזר holds that outside oil is fine. He holds it surely disqualifies; he only mentioned the two-לוגין case because it is the bigger surprise.

phrases.english: And רבי אליעזר is speaking in a 'no need to say' style:
no need to say that non-holy oil or another מנחה's oil disqualifies,
but if he set aside two לוגין for it,
since this one is fit for it
and that one is fit for it,
phrases.notes: Either לוג on its own could have been the proper oil for this מנחה.

phrases.english: I might say it should not disqualify –
so he teaches us that it does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רב זוטרא's attack, drops the step 28 suggestion, and answers the step 27 question in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: לא מיבעיא: the stated case is the bigger surprise, and the easier case is included in it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two לוגין that are each fit for this מנחה should not disqualify it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the מנחה's own two לוגין disqualify, and outside oil surely does.

steps.title: Where did רבי אליעזר learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what made רבי אליעזר read the משנה as the two-לוגין case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where does רבי אליעזר get this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אליעזר's reading. This question sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'too much oil' could mean many cases. The גמרא wants to know what in the משנה pushed רבי אליעזר to the two-לוגין case.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where does he know it?

phrases.english: And from where does רבי אליעזר get this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי אליעזר's reading, the גמרא asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the משנה shows that 'he increased its oil' means two לוגין of its own oil.

steps.title: The word 'its oil' in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה's wording 'its oil' bothered רבי אליעזר, and shows the case is about the מנחה's own oil, even two לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה was hard for him. Why does it say 'he increased its oil'? Let it say 'he increased oil for it'! Rather, it teaches us this: that even though he set aside two לוגין for it, it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. He shows that רבי אליעזר learned his reading from one small word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Its oil' means oil that belongs to this מנחה, not just any oil. Oil that belongs to the מנחה can only be 'too much' if he set aside more than one לוג for it. So the משנה is talking about two לוגין, just as רבי אליעזר said.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically? (why use this exact wording?)
He increased its oil (the משנה's words)

steps.whatToRemember: 'Too much oil' disqualifies a מנחה even when the oil is its own, two לוגין set aside for it. Outside oil disqualifies all the more. רבי אליעזר learned this from the word 'its' (שמנה) in the משנה.

phrases.english: רבא said: The משנה was difficult for him,
why specifically does it teach 'he increased its oil'?
Let it teach 'he increased oil for it'!
Rather, it teaches us this,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּהִפְרִישׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי לוּגִּין.
phrases.english: that even though he set aside two לוגין for it, it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה's word 'its oil' shows the case is the מנחה's own oil, meaning two לוגין set aside for it.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: how much לבונה must remain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the משנה's next case, 'he decreased its לבונה,' and brings a ברייתא. רבי יהודה says one קורט left is disqualified and two קרטין is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He decreased its לבונה.' The רבנן taught: If it was decreased and was left with one pinch, it is disqualified. With two pinches, it is fit. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the משנה's words 'he decreased its לבונה.' It brings a ברייתא to show how far the לבונה can go down, starting with רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is the smallest amount of לבונה a מנחה can have and still be fit. רבי יהודה sets the minimum at two pinches; one pinch alone is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A pinch, a tiny amount (plural: קרטין)

phrases.english: 'He decreased its frankincense.'
The רבנן taught:

phrases.aramaic: חָסְרָה וְעָמְדָה עַל קוֹרֶט אֶחָד – פְּסוּלָה,
phrases.english: if it was decreased and was left with one pinch – it is disqualified,
with two pinches – it is fit,
these are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the oil discussion and moves to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, לבונה reduced to one קורט is disqualified; two קרטין is fit.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: even one pinch is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees and says one קורט is still fit; only less than that is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: With one pinch, it is fit. Less than that, it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי שמעון's opposing view on the smallest amount of לבונה allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון lowers the minimum from two pinches to one. So the two תנאים disagree only about the case of exactly one קורט: רבי יהודה says disqualified, רבי שמעון says fit.
steps.whatToRemember: How little לבונה may be left: רבי יהודה says at least two קרטין, רבי שמעון says one קורט is enough.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון says:
with one pinch – it is fit,
less than that – it is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: עַל קוֹרֶט אֶחָד – כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, one קורט of לבונה is fit; less than that is disqualified.
